title: observability: automate Prometheus/Grafana + log shipping for Private installs
author: Sophie Martinez
description:
Motivation: Private customers need a repeatable, auditable observability baseline when installing Redwood Private. Previously observability setup was manual (silently differs per customer) which caused onboarding delays and inconsistent alerting/dashboards. This PR automates Prometheus + Grafana provisioning, log shipping (Fluent Bit -> internal S3/log-collector), baseline dashboards, and critical alert rules as part of the private installer.

What this PR does: consolidated automation across Helm, Terraform and installer scripts so a single `private-installer` flow can bring up a monitored stack that meets our support SLOs. Key pieces included: automated Helm chart for observability with opinionated defaults for resource requests/limits and RBAC; Terraform module to create S3/log-bucket, IAM roles and KMS keys for log encryption; Fluent Bit config for structured JSON log shipping and labels; Grafana provisioning for baseline dashboards (Private Inference Overview, Model Serving Latency, Node/GPU Utilization); Prometheus scrape configs and alert rules tuned for private environments; roll-forward/rollback hooks to preserve dashboards/alerts on upgrades.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind `observability.enabled` flag (default: true for new installs, can be turned off for air-gapped customers). For upgrades, the installer will detect existing Prometheus/Grafana instances and run a non-destructive migration path (export/import dashboards, no forced reload of alerts). We included a dry-run mode for Terraform parts and a `--skip-observability` flag for constrained environments.

Testing and validation: automated e2e test added to perf-canary that deploys a minimal private cluster in CI with observability enabled; helm lint and chart-testing added; integration tests validate that alerts fire on simulated high-latency and that dashboards contain expected panels. Manual validation performed in staging private cluster with KMS-backed S3.

Backward compatibility: non-breaking. Existing installs without observability remain untouched unless operator explicitly enables the feature.

References: Linear ENG-4120 (private observability baseline), ENG-4178 (installer upgrade/rollback automation).

review_thread: Evan Li (reviewer): Please add a note on the expected retention settings and cost implications in the README. Also ensure the default resource requests are conservative for 4vCPU/8GB nodes.
Author (Sophie Martinez): Added a retention section in installer/README.md and reduced default requests to conservative values. Left a note to operators to override via values.yaml.
Priya Nair (reviewer): The Terraform module creates an IAM role; can we scope it to least privilege? Also request KMS key policy example for enterprise customers.
Author (Sophie Martinez): Scoped IAM role permissions and added a KMS key policy example in variables.tf and README. Marked the KMS policy as optional for air-gapped installs.
Marco Ruiz (approver): Verified e2e staging run and alert firing simulation. Approved with minor nits fixed in follow-up commit.
CI Bot: helm lint failed on first run (missing chart annotations) then passed after chart metadata fix.
Maintainer (merge): Squash-merged into main after green CI and two approvals.
release_notes: Automated observability for Private installs: adds Helm chart for Prometheus/Grafana, Terraform module for log storage/KMS/IAM, Fluent Bit log shipping config, baseline dashboards and SLO alert rules. Feature is opt-out via observability.enabled flag. See installer/README.md for upgrade and rollback instructions.
additional_testing_notes: Staging run produced expected dashboards and alerts. Simulated high-latency spike triggered private-slo-high-latency alert; Fluent Bit delivered structured logs to S3 bucket with KMS encryption. Dry-run terraform validated resource plan in CI.
